editorial.marketOverview: Friday's shortened session ended with Nasdaq up 2.31%, SOX about 4.7% and Russell 2000 up 1.7%; AP reports Nasdaq gained 6.7% over the week. QQQ repository return was 2.69%, with exact underlying timestamp unverified. Broad participation supports the relief case, but the latest repository model describes mixed chip and mega-cap internals. No weekend cash-market response exists.
editorial.whatChanged: The latest repository report (2026-11-28 10:59 ET) lowers the model score from -12 to -24 and describes mixed semiconductor and mega-cap internals with positive breadth. This is a model reassessment, not evidence of new trading. Open Watch remains unchanged at 2026-11-28T02:31:23+00:00. The score deterioration warrants caution but does not independently establish a material three-session path change.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The latest model score is -24 rather than -12, consistent with a more cautious neutral outlook. Friday's reported 10Y and 2Y yields imply 22.6 bp using percentage yields without rescaling; WSJ separately reports 4.921% and 4.693%. VXN 33.34 and VIX 23.81 are historical dashboard values with unknown tick timestamps. Reuters reports Brent 95.44 and WTI 83.08 settlements; WSJ reports a December hike fully priced Friday. None is a fresh synchronized quote.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday tests whether Friday's broad rally survives normal liquidity and the pending Sunday OPEC+ decision. Tuesday manufacturing and labor releases can move rates, while reported Marvell and Credo earnings after close may shape Wednesday semiconductor trading. Wednesday ADP and labor tightness data add rate sensitivity; software earnings after close mainly affect the following session. Friday payrolls and December 8–9 Fed meeting are outside the horizon.
editorial.bullCase: A sustained positive SOX/QQQ relative return under normal liquidity, broad participation and easing yields would offset the weaker model score. Constructive semiconductor guidance and lower oil supply risk would reinforce the case.
editorial.bearCase: The weaker repository score raises caution but needs price confirmation. A reversal of Friday chip leadership, contracting breadth, renewed oil supply pressure or 10Y above 5% would favor a bearish reassessment.
editorial.watchNext: Watch the official OPEC+ decision, Sunday futures reopening and Monday matched-time equity, rates and volatility observations. Recheck Tuesday macro and chip earnings schedules and Wednesday employment data. Treat weekend news impact as prospective until markets reopen.
